subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Art of the Post-Mortem
description: Learn The Art of the Post-Mortem in one minute.

hook.text: After every major outage, the best companies write a post-mortem: what happened, why, and how to prevent it next time.

buildup.text: A good post-mortem is blameless. It focuses on systems, not individuals. People make mistakes; systems catch them.

discovery.text: Google, AWS, and Cloudflare publish public post-mortems. They build trust by showing they learn from failures.

twist.text: The hardest part isn't writing the post-mortem — it's following through on action items. Many get filed and forgotten.

climax.text: A culture that treats failures as learning opportunities improves faster than one that punishes mistakes.

punchline.text: Blame fixes nothing. Blameless post-mortems fix systems.

quiz.question: What makes a post-mortem effective?
options: It is blameless and focuses on system improvements rather than individual fault
It identifies and punishes the person who caused the failure
It is kept secret so competitors cannot learn about weaknesses

details.summary: Blameless post-mortems analyze what happened, why, and how to prevent recurrence without blaming individuals. Companies like Google and Cloudflare publish detailed post-mortems that share lessons across the industry and build transparency with customers.
details.whyItMatters: Post-mortems turn failures into organizational learning. Without blameless analysis, teams hide mistakes instead of fixing systemic issues, and the same failures recur.
takeaways: Blameless post-mortems focus on systems, not individuals
They identify root causes and preventive actions
Published post-mortems share lessons across the industry

faq.question: What should a post-mortem include?
faq.answer: A timeline of events, root cause analysis, contributing factors, customer impact assessment, detection and response evaluation, corrective actions with owners and deadlines, and lessons learned. It should be written collaboratively by everyone involved.

faq.question: Why should post-mortems be blameless?
faq.answer: Blame discourages honest reporting and analysis. If people fear punishment, they hide mistakes rather than learning from them. Blameless post-mortems focus on how the system allowed the failure rather than who caused it, leading to more effective preventive changes.
